title: Resurrection after death
intro: Barzakh and life in the grave, the resurrection and the Day of Gathering.

learn.text: Barzakh and life in the grave

learn.html: Death is the parting of the soul from the body. The body is buried in the earth and becomes earth again, from which it was made, and the soul moves into the barzakh and continues another stage of life. Barzakh is where human souls stay from death until the resurrection.

learn.title: The questions in the grave
learn.html: In the grave the angels Munkar and Nakir will ask every person: Who is your Lord? Who is your Prophet? What is your religion? How a person answers depends on whether they were a believer in this world. Believing souls will have a pleasant place; the souls of unbelievers will feel suffering in the grave.
The Prophet (SAW) used to make this dua: “My Lord, protect me from the punishment of the Fire and the punishment of the grave.” (Bukhari)

Many hadiths name sins that bring punishment in the grave, among them: carrying tales and backbiting, praying without being properly clean, leaving Salah or not caring about it, lying, not paying zakah, stealing, betrayal, spreading trouble among Muslims, taking interest, refusing to help the wronged, and drinking alcohol.

Allah will command the angel Israfil to blow the trumpet a second time, and people will be brought back to life out of their graves – Allah tells us that the souls will be joined with their bodies again. (Qur’an, At-Takwir 81:7)

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Someone asked: “Who will give life to bones when they have crumbled?” Allah answers: say, “He will give them life who made them the first time, and He knows every creation.” <small>(Qur’an, Ya-Sin 36:78–79)</small>

Belief in life after death is a basic truth of Islam. The One who made us the first time is able to do it a second time. In many places the Qur’an shows this is reasonable, because it has examples in our life on earth and in nature, which is also Allah’s work.

learn.text: The Mahshar – the place of gathering

learn.html: All people, from Adam (AS) to the end of the world, will rise from their graves and go to the place of gathering, the Mahshar – a wide, flat plain with nowhere to hide. No one will look at anyone else. The sun will come close, and people will sweat according to their disobedience – some up to the ankles, some to the knees, some to the throat. As hard as it is for those who denied and sinned, it will be calm and peaceful for the believers. The day of the gathering is called the Day of Mahshar.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: When the deafening blast comes, a person will flee from their brother, mother, father, wife and children – each will be busy with themselves. Some faces that Day will be bright, laughing and joyful; others will be covered in dust and darkness. <small>(Qur’an, ‘Abasa 80:33–42)</small>

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Scientists have found that one small part of the human body never decays: a little bone at the end of the spine, called the tailbone.
